citation: Olson, C. B., Woodworth, K., Arshan, N., Black, R., Chung, H. Q., D'Aoust, C., Dewar, T., Friedrich, L., Godfrey, L., Land, R., Matuchniak, T., Scarcella, R., & Stowell, L. (2020). The pathway to academic success: Scaling up a text-based analytical writing intervention for Latinos and English learners in secondary school. Journal of Educational Psychology, 112(4), 701-717. https://doi.org/10.1037/edu0000387
report_number: Pathway to Academic Success Project (i3 Validation grant); independent evaluation by SRI International. WWC study/intervention: Pathway Project.
design: Multisite cluster RCT. Assignment level = Teacher/Class (teachers randomized together with their focal class within school-by-grade blocks). 230 secondary ELA/ELD teachers (113 treatment, 117 control) from 40 schools across 7 districts affiliated with 4 National Writing Project sites in southern California. Grades 7-12. Control = business-as-usual (delayed treatment). Subject = text-based analytical writing (ELA). Two student outcomes: (1) NWP Analytic Writing Continuum for Literary Analysis (AWC-LA) on-demand writing assessment (researcher/developer-made); (2) Smarter Balanced (SBAC) state standardized ELA assessment (standardized/independent).
problems: Source is a legal green-OA copy from eScholarship (UC Irvine Previously Published Works, identical to the published JEP article; DOI 10.1037/edu0000387). The paper reports effect sizes directly as 'd' (SRI's standardized ITT impact estimates) with SEs and Kenward-Roger degrees of freedom from multilevel models; outcomes were standardized within cohort/prompt and the impact is 'standardized within the analytic sample', so these d's are the model-based SMD. Hedges' g = J*d using the model dof. Separate arm-level n_t / n_c are NOT reported: the paper gives only TOTAL analytic student N per analysis (AWC-LA N=894; SBAC N=2,733) and randomization-block / teacher counts; n_t and n_c left null. ICC not reported as a design-effect ICC (only an MDES<=.15 power assumption is mentioned, p.21) -> icc left null per spec (never guess). Estimates already account for clustering (random effects at student/teacher/block) so cluster_adjusted=true; recording n_clusters as teacher N (the randomized unit). Models include student-level baseline (pretest) control -> pretest_adjusted=true. The meta-analysis coded this study as 'External' (independent) test type / 'Short' (Year-1) duration; the SBAC standardized ELA contrast is the independent-measure outcome the review would have used (mapped to Reading), while the AWC-LA writing assessment is the researcher/developer-made writing outcome (mapped to Other). Both extracted and labeled; central filtering selects on test_type. The four AWC-LA analytic attributes (content/structure/fluency/conventions) are subscales of the holistic AWC-LA composite and are extracted as outcome_role=subscale. Timepoint = end of Year 1 (immediate post; the impact analyses use the Year-1 wave).

effect_sizes.timepoint: post (end of Year 1, spring SBAC; CST used as baseline)
effect_sizes.g_method: Paper reports d=0.06, s.e.=0.05 from multilevel ITT model (SBAC & CST standardized within analytic sample by grade). g = J*d, J=1-3/(4*83-1)=0.99094 (dof=83 Kenward-Roger), g=0.0595; g_se = J*0.05 = 0.0495; g_var = g_se^2 = 0.002455. Standardized within the analytic sample (grade-standardized SBAC scores).

effect_sizes.notes: Independent/standardized achievement transfer measure (the meta-analysis 'External' test type). Non-significant (p>.10), positive. Total student n=2,733; teacher n=134; block n=51 (n_clusters=teacher n=134, the randomized unit). reading/ELA -> Reading.
